A message that Thunderbird is not responding frequently means you have an Anti-Virus which is scanning every file that gets opened.   • https://www.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/all/

then it's likely the Thunderbird folder that needs being make exempt from scanning is here because that would be the default location for storing everything to do with your profile.

  • C:Users/username/Appdata/Roaming/Thunderbird

content:
Gmail stores all your email - incoming, outgoing, archived, spam everything in one folder called 'All Mail'.

Gmail understands that's useless for general use. They invented 'labels' which work like a tag on each email in 'All Mail'. The applied label means emails can be displayed in a view that looks more like normal folders. If you logon to the gmail webmail account and look in 'All Mail' you will see each email will have an appropriate 'label' applied. If no label then it means it's archived.

Thunderbird has no concept of 'labels'. It access the label/folder on server eg: Inbox and downloads a copy of anything displaying in server 'Inbox' label.

If you look at emails in 'All Mail' folder in Thunderbird, you see it does not display the labels.

If anything is deleted from 'All Mail' , it means it will be deleted off server, those deleted emails will disappear from whatever imap folder they were in because they will not exist on server. I would advise you never do anything in an 'All Mail' folder.

In Thunderbird, unsubscribe from seeing 'All Mail'. In gmail webmail account accessed via a browser: Settings > See all settings > selects 'Labels' tab and in System Labels section - 'All Mail' uncheck the 'Show in imap' checkbox.

Do this:

  • The User name = full comcast email address
  • Click on 'Edit'
  • In 'Description' field type the same email address as shown in User Name'
  • Click on OK

Now select the second smtp It should have a different User name = email address for another mail account.

  • Click on 'Edit'
  • In 'Description' field type the same email address as shown in User Name'
  • Click on OK

Repeat for all four smtps So each smtp = one for each mail account. Each one will have a different User name.

Now check each mail account is using the correct SMTP for that account.

  • In Account Setting
  • Left Pane select name of account/email address
  • Look bottom right pane for 'Outgoing Server (SMTP)'

It should now display the info/username/email address you put in 'Description' The email address should match the same one as the selected mail account. If it does not match - :

  • Click on the drop down icon to see list and select the correct smtp which has correct email address.

DO NOT click on on 'EDIT SMTP_server' button because if it's pointing to wrong one you can mess up the smtp of another account.

Please repeat for each mail account - each account must use the smtp specifically for that mail account.

content:
If you are viewing the same account on various folders, then I presume the account is set up as an IMAP mail account.

So, All emails are saved on the server and you use various computers to access that same email address/account on the server.

If you are only seeing a restricted set of emails then it's possible you have a filter operating on that folder. eg: Quick Filter enabled and eg: 'Show only unread mail' selected Please check - is any icon selected in the Quick Filter and that includes the pin icon if yes then click on it to remove the filter.

You say: I can see all my Emails of years past, But you not say whether those emails are in Inbox or other folders. It would be reasonable to presume they are not still in the Inbox, but have been organised into other folders or even put into 'Archives' folders.

Is it possible you do not see all the necessary imap folders? In Folder Pane

  • Right click on the imap mail account name folder and select 'Subscribe'
  • Click on 'Refresh'
  • Select all the required folders
  • click on 'OK'

You say : mails of about the last four weeks are accessible and probably saved, be it in the default folder or a local one.

A default folder for the mail account would be Inbox, Drafts, Templates, Sent, Archives, Spam, Trash All other folders in the imap account would be created by you, but they are still imap folders.

A local one - that implies not in the Imap account but in the 'Local Folders' account.

Can you be more specific. It sounds like you are saying the missing emails are not just one folder and not just one account.

When posting a question please supply info about the computer etc: What OS are using ? What version of Thunderbird are you using ? Are you talking about an IMAP account or a POP account ? Are missing emails in the IMAP account or the POP account or Local Folders account ?

It would also be useful to upload images to help explain situation, eg: one image showing computer A that has emails and one image B showing the computer that is missing emails. Then it's possible to compare the two views.

content:
Go very carefully here. IMAP is a problem in your situation. You could easily lose it all. First, be sure you know where the IMAP account's folders are on your computer. Here are suggested steps:

  1. click help>troubleshootinginformation
  2. scroll to 'profile folder' and click 'open folder'
  3. EXIT thunderbird
  4. you are now in profile, click the Imapmail folder and then click desired IMAP account folder
  5. look for sets of files, such as inbox, inbox.msf, sent, sent.msf, etc. Ignore the msf entries, and COPY (not move) the inbox, sent, and other such entries and PASTE them to the Mail\Local Folders folder.
  6. restart thunderbird and review that all messages are in Local Folders.

If you are uncomfortable doing that, then do the first two steps up to the act of copying and write down the exact disk location, probably something such as c:\users\<yourid>\appdata\roaming\thunderbird\profiles\<profile name>\imapmail\<IMAPaccount name>\inbox

  1. Now, install the addon 'importexporttools NG'
  2. highlight Local Folers and rightclick
  3. select the importexport option to import mbox file
  4. now, locate one of the IMAP account files (again, ignore msf entries) and select ok.
  5. repeat for each file to be imported
  6. you should now see the messages in local folder

Regardless of approach, once you have all the message folders in Local Folders you can safely delete the old account. Had you ever been able to access that server, all the messages would likely have disappeared as IMAP syncs to the server.

If in doubt on what to do, post screenshot of the IMAP account folder.
